features.method: Square of side 120 m, diagonal oriented north-south (both facts from the H.E.S.S. Telescopes page), computed by placing one vertex at each of bearings 0/90/180/270 degrees and distance 120*sqrt(2)/2 = 84.8528 m (spherical destination-point formula, R = 6371008.8 m) from the array's own official published coordinate (site:khomas-highland-hess, precision_m 200). accuracy_m is set equal to that anchor's own precision_m (200 m), satisfying the coarse-anchor rule exactly rather than claiming a false sub-200 m accuracy for where the square sits; the square's own shape (120 m side) is exact by construction from the sourced figure. No OpenStreetMap trace of the individual CT1-CT4 telescope pads could be attempted this session (Overpass refused every connection attempt, see worklog), which would otherwise have anchored the square far more tightly.
features.name: H.E.S.S. CT1-CT4 telescope square (120 m side, diagonal north-south)

provenance.locator: H.E.S.S. Telescopes page, array layout paragraph
provenance.note: Confidence 'derived' per contract (a derived shape is derived, even with a passing check).
provenance.quote: The initial four H.E.S.S. telescopes (Phase I) are arranged in form of a square with 120 m side length. The diagonal of the square is oriented north-south.

features.method: CT5 (the 28 m dish added in 2012) stands 'at the center of the array' per the H.E.S.S. Telescopes page; reuses the array's own published coordinate (23d16'18"S 16d30'00"E, site:khomas-highland-hess) verbatim as CT5's own position rather than computing/guessing an offset. No CT5-specific coordinate distinct from the array's own point was published this session.
features.name: H.E.S.S. CT5 telescope (centre of the array)

provenance.locator: H.E.S.S. Telescopes page; H.E.S.S. Site page
provenance.note: 'verified': representation is 'surveyed' from a rank<=10 official source.
provenance.quote: an single huge dish with about 600 m2 mirror area was added at the center of the array

summary.plain: The H.E.S.S. gamma-ray telescope array on Farm Göllschau in the Khomas Highland of Namibia: four 12 m telescopes on a 120 m square plus the large central CT5 dish.
